witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it.

Solana's legacy packet maximum is 1,232 bytes (PACKET_DATA_BYTES), and as of 2026-09-02 NO transaction in this campaign is over it -- so this witness carries no exclusion list at all, and that is the whole change. Its predecessor named the two families that WERE over: the full-width Structured actions and the hostiles shaped like them, which carry K asset rows and K materialized account quadruples; and every Trading common-Hot frame, which carries the Trading envelope and its own outer account frame on top of the Claims one. Physical ABI v3 closed both. An exclusion list is a standing promise that some frame is allowed to be broken, and it is the first thing to delete when it stops being true: kept any longer it would have hidden a regression inside the families it excused.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select((.label | startswith("Trading common-Hot")) | not) | select(.label | test("IssueStructured|UnwrapStructured|issue against|unwrap against")) | .wire_bytes] | max | tostring
witnesses.provenance: THE MEASUREMENT, on the CLAIMS-DIRECT frame; the Hot route's extents are pinned by rational-representation-v2-the-common-hot-frame-extents-are-pinned and this query excludes them. A v0 message carrying IssueStructured or UnwrapStructured at K = 3, compiled against a real activated Address Lookup Table and carrying the set_compute_unit_limit a real transaction always pays, is 1,005 bytes against a 1,232-byte limit -- INSIDE it by 227. It was 1,397 until physical ABI v3, which is -392 exactly: the three re-derived per-coordinate PDAs left the asset row (-288 at K = 3) and the header became action-conditional (structured 488 -> 384). THE QUERY CHANGED SHAPE with the number. It used to select on `wire_bytes > 1232`, which is a filter that silently returns null the day nothing is over -- and null is not a byte count, it is the absence of one, so the witness would have gone red saying 'expected 1397, chain says null' and told a reader nothing about what the frame now costs. It selects on the LABEL now and reports the extent unconditionally. Re-pinned 2026-09-02 by STRUCTURED from a green 47-test campaign run on real ELFs.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | test("terminal|Denominate|Reconstitute|replay|namespace|lookup table")) | select((.label | test("Issue|issue|Unwrap|unwrap")) | not) | select((.label | startswith("Trading common-Hot")) | not) | .wire_bytes] | max | (. <= 1232) | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The selected-outcome actions -- Denominate, Reconstitute, RedeemTerminal -- carry asset_count == 1 at every K, so their request is 488 + 160 bytes at any representation width and their CLAIMS-DIRECT frames fit with room. So a K = 3 Structured product can be denominated, reconstituted and redeemed on a cluster and can never be issued or unwrapped there; this witness is the half of that sentence the previous packet witness used to cover for the whole campaign. It excludes the Trading common-Hot rows ON PURPOSE and does not weaken to do it: those frames do NOT fit, they are pinned to the byte by the extent witness below, and folding them in here would replace two exact statements with one false one. It also excludes the FULL-WIDTH labels that happen to match this pattern: `IssueStructured before a replay close` is a K = 3 issuance at 1,397 bytes that carries the word `replay` because of what it is planted for, and it belongs to the structured family this witness is the complement of. A label pattern is a coarse instrument; the two exclusions are what keep it from claiming the wrong half.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | startswith("Trading common-Hot")) | select((.label | test("lookup table")) | not) | .wire_bytes] | unique | join(",")
witnesses.provenance: THE MEASUREMENT, on the route a browser actually drives. Three extents, each a v0 message against a live Address Lookup Table with the set_compute_unit_limit a real transaction always pays: Denominate 1,049, RedeemTerminal 1,137, IssueStructured 1,197 (the last carried by two transactions, the commit and the substituted-digest hostile, which is why the list is de-duplicated). ALL THREE ARE NOW UNDER Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES -- by 183, 95 and 35 -- so every action of this family is submittable on the common-Hot route at the K = 3 campaign basis. They were 1,253 / 1,277 / 1,589 and none of them was. The lever was NOT the one this provenance first named: dropping the three re-derived per-coordinate PDAs is -288 at K = 3 and lands IssueStructured at 1,301, still over. Physical ABI v3 pairs that with an action-conditional header (structured 488 -> 384, selected -> 380, terminal -> 444) and it is the PAIR that closes the route. Recorded as exact equalities rather than as 'fits': a bound that only says the route works cannot report the day it stops. Re-pinned 2026-09-02 by STRUCTURED from a green 47-test campaign run on real ELFs -- the first figures here that are executed extents rather than arithmetic on a measured request delta.
A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This asserts that no transaction in this campaign is unmeasured.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims -- named or unnamed_refusal -- is a program decision, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about a program.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | endswith("commits")) | .logs[] | select(. == "Program TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb success")] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: This campaign's Token-2022 fixture is the byte-for-byte canonical, cross-host-reproducible spl-token-2022 11.0.0 ELF pinned in programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/fixtures/token-2022-v11.provenance (SHA-256 e2acdfb750881462ad613a15cc9c54ae17ce066580e867e1e635fbdfe01f5697), authenticated at TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb -- Solana's real, deployed Token-2022 program address, which only the canonical artifact can occupy under the fixture's own digest check. This counts the runtime's own success logs for it across the NINE committing transactions, and the count is a function of the campaign basis width K. Claims-direct, thirteen: IssueStructured 4 (K = 3 shard transfers plus the receipt mint), UnwrapStructured 4 (the receipt burn plus K shard transfers), Denominate 1, Reconstitute 1, winning terminal 2, losing terminal 1. Trading common-Hot, seven more: IssueStructured 4, Denominate 1, RedeemTerminal 2 -- the same per-action counts, because the Hot route changes who invokes Claims and not what Claims does with Token-2022. It was eleven at K = 2 and thirteen before the common-Hot route committed anything; it moves with K by design, so a silent width change fails here.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims rational-representation-v2: caller refuses after a complete terminal redemption") | (if .error == null then "committed" else ([.logs[] | select(. == "Program GCkWCknJ46pyPNHC9DPjTxedvjLHYJUVioxe7X5o6xa4 success")] | length | tostring) end)
witnesses.provenance: A rollback case is only evidence if the thing being rolled back actually happened. This asserts, from the runtime's own log, that a transaction the ledger records as FAILED contains a completed Claims invocation (which itself only returns after real Custody and real Token-2022 both succeeded, per the terminal redemption's own account frame). The `if .error == null` guard makes a campaign that accidentally let the transaction commit fail this witness rather than pass it.

The budgets live in tools/gauntlet/CU_BUDGETS.json; this witness carries no number of its own. The independent value is Solana's 1,400,000 per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT. This campaign carried no CU witness at all until the wallet payout landed, which is why its three rows are the only ones named: they are the first routes a WALLET reaches on its own, so a regression here is a regression a user meets rather than one a keeper absorbs. Every transaction a budget row names is a LITERAL label the recorder emits; the wildcards in bindings.json are the census's and must never be copied into a budget, which would make the row AMBIGUOUS.
